work.title: Encomium and Martyrdom of Helias (Coptic)

paragraphs.text: Jesus ✠ Christ. An encomium by our holy father Apa Stephen, honored in every way, bishop of the city of Hnes, which he delivered on the day of the holy martyr of Christ Jesus, Apa Elias, which is the eleventh of Pashons, while they were celebrating his feast in his shrine in peace. Amen.
There are trees that grow in distant lands. Even though we have never seen them face to face, by enjoying their fruits we come to know their beauty and their sweetness.

So it is with the prize-bearing martyrs who lived in every city and every land. We did not go with them to the tribunal, nor did we watch the contest they endured for Christ. Yet through the many gifts of grace in their shrines we come to know their greatness and their honor before the Lord. So it truly is with our chosen crown-bearer, the exalted prize-bearer, the holy Elias, who is the reason for our gathering today, O pious ones. O prize-bearer Elias, luminous in name and in virtue alike, I see the holy saying of our Savior fulfilled in you: "Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father."
It is [?]
But
So it truly is with our chosen crown-bearer, the exalted prize-bearer, the holy Elias, who is the reason for our gathering today, O pious ones.
O prize-bearer Elias, luminous in name and in virtue alike,
I see the holy saying of our Savior fulfilled in you: "Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father."
Christ said this, of course, about all the righteous.
But the holy Elias resembled the sun in his name and his virtue, and in his light, through what his name means.
For the meaning of "Elias", taken as Greek, is "the sun".
First a name comes with birth, at the same moment: the name of the flesh.
After that his way of life became manifest and confirmed the name.
So the honor of his blessing also matches the name of this saint, as it is written in the Psalms. But the sun is a thing of the senses, and its light comes to an end.
But the sun is a thing of the senses, and its light comes to an end.
The light of the martyrs, however, is imperishable.
The sun sets, and rises again.
The prize-bearing martyrs set in the body through their death,
but they come with the Lord in glory, with the crown of their sufferings set upon them.
But let us come to the reason for our gathering today, the commemoration of the holy Elias, who steered his soldiering well, like a good charioteer.
Elias, truly a general of the King, Christ, and the physician of all who are sick.
Now this man was not a laborer, one of those who work the land, nor did he eat his bread by the sweat of his face.
Nor
Nor did he live his life in poverty, so that you could say the hardship of poverty drove him to run into this stadium of martyrdom.
No, he was well-born, one of those high in rank.
He was rich, one of the notable men.
He was [?] in the graces, a lover of Christ.
He was a warrior beyond measure against visible enemies;
he was a victor beyond measure over the hidden evil adversaries.
He was close to the king of this world,
and he is a friend of the King of heaven and earth, Christ Jesus.
They enrolled him for soldiering in the earthly ranks;
they also enrolled him in the valor of heaven through the contest of confession.
His [?]
And now he has become a healer of those who draw near to him and of those [?].
Beautiful is the stadium of your martyrdom, O truly noble one.
Your crown does not fade;
countless are the fruits of your righteousness.
To whom among the saints shall I compare you, O holy Elias?
I will compare you to the one who bears the same name as you, Elijah,
who was taken up by whirlwinds and chariots of fire,
who shut the sky and opened it again by the word of his mouth.
For that Elijah fasted forty days and forty nights.
O this great wonder-worker! Yet after he had burned up the two captains of fifty and their hundred soldiers,
and after he had slain the priests of Baal, four hundred [?] in number,
in the end he fled for fear of the threat of a harlot woman.
But you, O victory-bearer, prize-bearer, God-bearer, Spirit-bearer, and crown-bearer of the New Covenant, honored martyr, faithful noble one,
honored martyr,
faithful noble one,
unconquered athlete,
victorious contender,
holy Elias: you stood before the threats of kings,
you trampled on the power of the fire,
you stood strong in the war against your enemies.
I will compare you to the wise Daniel.
He stood before the kings of the Chaldeans;
and so did you, O honored athlete.
He despised the decrees of Darius and Cyrus;
you too, O crown-bearer of Christ, despised the idolaters.
They threw Daniel into the lions' den because he did not obey the decree of the Persians and the Medes.
But you, O righteous one, endured not only the ordeal of the beasts for the confession of Christ,
but you stood strong in many contests. I will compare you to the beloved physician and sage, Luke the evangelist.
I will
You became like him in following Christ and in becoming a martyr for him.
So I will paint for you the story of the holy Elias. Shall I speak of the grace that came to him from the Lord,
or shall I tell of his struggle for God,
or rather of the help of the Most High, which helped you?
Shall I tell of the rage and madness of the tyrant, or of the endurance of this holy martyr?
He was like a sheep among wolves;
he was like a lily among thorns.
He was a light among those in the darkness of the error of idols. Those people lived in luxury, but this noble man was held in check by God.
But this noble man was held in check by God.
They worshiped the things their own hands had made; but the holy Elias worshiped the only Creator, who is God.
And the world-ruler of darkness kept urging him toward the things of darkness.
But the noble martyr had his citizenship in heaven.
Picture, then, the splendid theater full of grace:
a single man, not yet a saint, standing in the midst, before God
and men, among angels and demons [?].
The earthly ones were forcing him to sacrifice to the earthly gods,
while the King of heaven, Christ, was strengthening his noble one for the contest.
"Will you sacrifice then, Elias, or not?" he said.
The holy martyr said, "I am a physician; I heal others.
How could I bear to let my own soul fall sick with idolatry?
I am a soldier in the earthly army, but I do not wish to be cut off from the armies of the angels.
I am a citizen of a city on earth, but from this day on I will choose for myself the Jerusalem of heaven, the truly existing holy city."
What, then, will the powers of darkness do now?
What will the king who fights against God do?
He flattered;
he threatened;
he pleaded;
he raged;
and, to put it briefly,
the rains came down,
the rain fell on them, the winds blew.
They blew
and beat against the mind of this saint, but they could not shake him, because he was founded on the unshakable rock, Christ. Then, since the first trial was over,
then, since the first trial was over,
they called the athlete and [?] of truth into the contest.
Again there were sufferings, very great ones;
again many public punishments and tortures;
again the [?] of the executioners;
again, from strength to strength,
from one ruler to another,
from one tribunal to another,
from cruel sufferings to many afflictions.
For the weapons of his soldiering were not fleshly, but powers of God.
He showed that he was following Christ, who stood before the high priest, Herod and Pilate.
For the wise are wont to say:
But this holy martyr, the holy Elias, as he showed himself in the first ordeal, and in the second and the third,
therefore his crown became splendid in heaven and on earth. He went through fire and water, but the place of rest is laid up for him, as the Psalmist says.
He went through fire and water, but the place of rest is laid up for him, as the Psalmist says.
They hung him on a tree, but this was so that he might resemble his teacher, who was crucified for us.
He renounced his [?], their will, and perishable pleasure,
but the banquet of the kingdom of heaven is prepared for him.
He left behind these temporary ranks, but the boundless good things are his.
He turned his face away from the kings of the earth,
but [?] the vision of the light of the holy consubstantial Trinity.
They took off his head with the sword, but he went to his true head, Christ. He renounced the king's military belt, but became like David, who threw Saul's armor off himself.
Women came out to meet David, dancing for his victory over the foreigner.
But for this noble man, angels were his judges in the games, because he conquered the father of all foreigners, that is, the devil.
You are blessed now, O prize-bearer.
Beautiful is your victory, O you who went through many contests for love of God.
And the Lord will crown you with the crown of righteousness.
Now let no one lose faith on hearing of all the sufferings this prize-bearing martyr endured for Christ.
For great is the number of healings that take place every day in his shrine.
They spread out over everyone, almost like the rays of the shining sun.
How many, then, are the healings of the sick,
the castings-out of demons,
those who had come near the gates of death and whom he brings back to life again in this way, through the intercessions he makes for us before the Lord Jesus!
For he knows how to heal those with dropsy by the art of his medicine, without payment.
He knows how to heal the sick, removing what [?] in their limbs.
In short, this saint heals everyone, receiving grace from God and giving each person what he asks, fulfilling the request of every one who comes to his holy shrine.
fulfilling the request of every one who comes to his holy shrine.
You see that he is a patron for life to whoever has him, fighting for us against the hidden enemies,
and also a healer of our bodies.
For indeed the very day of his death is fitting for this weighty subject.
For wise physicians say of this month, Pashons, that it is a month that by its nature brings on sickness,
because in it the trees put out their leaves.
For it was at that time that God went down to Egypt to bring the children of Israel out of their midst with signs and wonders.
In this same month, too, the [?] of day and night comes about, the two being equal to each other.
So it is fitting
that his holy prayers should bring relief to everyone who is sick in soul and body.
This much I have set before your love about the contest of this noble martyr, the holy Elias.
Now, my beloved, I wish to say a word of praise about the holy brothers whose bones are laid in his shrine,
for it is a good thing.
The wise Solomon also says: "Three are those that walk well."
That is why the Lord rightly ordained that the bones of these three saints should rest beside one another,
so that the holy Trinity, for which they contended, might be glorified in the naming of these three holy ones.
You, then, now, O pious people, children of grace, who wish to run well and to win the kingdom of Christ: it is good that you be eager to come to this place today, and also every day.
But let no one seek only the healing of his body and neglect the sins of his soul.

Look at the sufferings the martyrs underwent: shut up in prisons, lying on the ground with their blood running onto the earth, hungry and thirsty, their bodies full of wounds, because they did not stop praying to God night and day. O what great shame, that we sleep with slackened hearts and do not reckon for ourselves the sufferings the saints underwent until they were found worthy of life! Above all the Lord of the saints, Jesus, kept watch at night in prayer, not for his own sake, God forbid, but for our sake, wretched as we are, to teach us the way to be saved from the snares of the evil one. See how empty everything in this world is. What do we gain by celebrating the feast of the martyrs, who contended against sin unto death for the faith of the Son of God,
O what great shame, that we sleep with slackened hearts and do not reckon for ourselves the sufferings the saints underwent until they were found worthy of life!

Above all the Lord of the saints, Jesus, kept watch at night in prayer, not for his own sake, God forbid, but for our sake, wretched as we are, to teach us the way to be saved from the snares of the evil one.
See how empty everything in this world is.
What do we gain by celebrating the feast of the martyrs, who contended against sin unto death for the faith of the Son of God,
while we ourselves are full of passions of every kind and sins of many sorts, and do not repent before the messenger comes for us?

Little is the time [?]. He comes face to face and tests [?] to see what kind it is, lest he find there is no flour inside it, that is, deeds full of every virtue, but only the outward look of the husk, which is hypocrisy.
lest he find there is no flour inside it, that is, deeds full of every virtue, but only the outward look of the husk, which is hypocrisy.
For the name and the rank we bear are one thing, and the deeds we do in secret are another,
as it is written: "The things they do in secret it is shameful even to speak of."
Woe to the man who gives place to Satan so that he dwells in him through the desire for defilement, because he did not [?] while he was alive.
And if he dies before repenting, he will be in the place of eternal punishment, and he will not find [?]. See, it is said that there were some of his disciples whom he would send to preach.
See
The evangelist Luke says that he gave them authority to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every disease and every sickness.
The good thing is that when the unclean spirits, which are the defiled thoughts, are cast out of a man, he is healed in soul and body.

O man, cast these passions out of your soul, the very ones we love above all, and you will be saved from the undying worm in Amente. Drive away from you the desire of the flesh that wars against the Spirit, and they will not cast you out of the heavenly dwelling places.
Drive away from you the desire of the flesh that wars against the Spirit, and they will not cast you out of the heavenly dwelling places.
Let the honor we pay the martyrs not consist only in coming into their shrine,
but let us become like them in their strength; let us hold fast to their endurance.
Let
Let us strive to match their love for God. They conquered the world and all its desires; let us not allow the world and its will to conquer us. They despised the threat of tortures;
We
they won for themselves the friendship of heaven;
let us too place our citizenship there.
For this is how we shall become friends.
And if we do not live out a martyrdom like the holy Elias, let us at least live righteously like the brothers beside him.
But

This too comes from the wisdom of God: he arranged for the bones of the ascetics to lie beside those of the martyr, so that their example might urge everyone toward repentance. So if you live in a time of persecution, here is the one who conquered in the persecutions, the holy Elias. And again, if you live without persecution, here are those who were proven in their way of life and ascetic practice. For indeed the ascetic life is [?] and falls no short of martyrdom. And to show that this is so, I will bring you the wise apostle as an advocate for this point, from when he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints,
So if you live in a time of persecution, here is the one who conquered in the persecutions, the holy Elias. And again, if you live without persecution,
Again
For
And
when he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints,

and when he came to Gideon, Barak, Samson, David and Samuel. He set down those who conquered in the stadium of martyrdom, and joined to them the monastic life, saying: "They wandered in deserts and mountains, and caves and holes in the earth, in want, afflicted, suffering, of whom the world was not worthy."
"They wandered in deserts and mountains, and caves and holes in the earth, in want, afflicted, suffering, of whom the world was not worthy."
And at the end he crowned them all with the name of martyrdom, saying: "Therefore, since we have this great crowd of witnesses set around us, let us run with endurance the contest set before us."
You see that the monastic life is the sister of martyrdom, for the one who lives it without hypocrisy and without falsehood.
For indeed Christ himself prefigured these two contests for us in his own person.
He conquered the devil when he withdrew into the desert;

and again he established the salvation of the whole world through the victory of the cross. To those in the desert he gave victory by becoming their leader in this; and to those who rushed into the stadium of martyrdom he became a crown.
Again
And we too, my brothers, let us follow the Lord and what belongs to the Lord. Let us confess the Lord together with the holy martyrs.
Let
Let us become holy for him, like those who purified themselves for him through ascetic practice; let us guard our faith like the holy martyrs.
Let
Let us become sharers in the love of the Spirit.
For even if we cannot shine like the sun, let us at least be seen in the rank of the stars.

What I mean is this: even if we cannot attain the greatness of the martyrs' contests, let us at least be found in the order of the faithful. Even if we cannot love God as he loved us, let us love one another as ourselves.
But
Even if
And even if we have nothing to give a poor man, comfort him with your words; strengthen him with the promise of the kingdom of heaven.
Tell him the apostle's saying: "The sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed to us."
For poverty is a martyrdom for the one who bears it with thanksgiving.
For this is what Christ, the life of us all, said: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."
And those who were persecuted for righteousness' sake are the ones who will be called sons of God, that is, the martyrs.
And we, my beloved, let us love our neighbors as the martyrs loved God and shed their blood for him, so that we may find mercy on the day when we hasten to stand before him.
May the Lord bless you all, from the least of you to the greatest, and raise you up out of this negligence.

Be sober and keep watch, for the adversary, the devil, walks in darkness night and day, and we do not see him as he seeks to devour our souls. I beseech you all: let each of you examine his life, whether he has strayed or is sound. If he has sinned, let him repent of what he has done, and I trust in God and in the prayers of the holy martyr, the holy Elias, that he will forgive him.
I beseech
If

Let us not linger day after day, until the messenger of death overtakes us and finds us unprepared, and we regret it and curse the day on which we were born in vain. For the time has slipped away from us, and your door has been [?]. Whatever state one is found in at that hour, whether good or evil, that hour has gone by.
For the time has slipped away from us, and your door has been [?]. Whatever state one is found in at that hour, whether good or evil, that hour has gone by.
[?] It is good for us to repent before they shut the door of repentance on us.
May our God, Christ Jesus, the Lord of heaven and earth, lay his peace upon us and drive the devil and his demons away from us.
To him be glory and honor and worship, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, the perfect Trinity in unity and the unity in consubstantial Trinity, for ever and ever. Amen.

Jesus ✠ Christ. This is the martyrdom of the holy martyr of Christ, Apa Elias, who completed his honoured contest, together with those who were with him, on the eleventh day of the month of Paremhotep, in peace. Amen.

Now when the apostles had completed their preaching according to the command of our Saviour Jesus, they spread [?] the Church from the rising of the sun to its setting, so that its sweet fragrance and their offering reached to heaven, and their hearts too were set straight toward the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And the name of God was glorified, and Mastema was put to shame.
The glory of the Church was revealed, and the idols ceased, until two hundred and forty-six [?] years had passed since the ascension of our Saviour Jesus Christ the Lord,

while the whole world was of one faith, worshipping one God, Jesus Christ, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen. And it happened [?] And it happened, a long [?] long time after this, that the world sinned by worshipping idols.
And it happened
And when Mastema saw that he had been put to shame, together with all who were his,

he took counsel with those who were his, saying, "What shall we do, so that I may turn the world back to me once more and they may listen to me?" He devised crooked thoughts in this way, so that he might make the world turn aside as it had at first. Likewise, it is necessary that the martyrs receive the crown.
A

He took counsel within himself, saying, "I will enter into the hearts of the great kings who rule the world and turn their hearts, so that I may make them forsake the God of heaven, worship idols and shed blood, and also do confused works that profit nothing [?]."

These are the names of the kings who ruled at that time, each one in his own country: first, Liberianus, king of Konoia; [?] Nicomedes, king of Persia; third, Eutychodorus, king of Media; Diocletian, king of the Romans; Herodian, king of Thentike [?].
When the devil had led them astray, they forsook the God of heaven, worshipped idols, and shed the blood of all the Christians, each in his own country.
Now there was one named Soterichus, who was the Caesar of Herodian, the king of Thentike.

When he saw that they were abusing all the Christians because of the holy name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and since he also saw great miracles that had come about through them, he too turned away from the idols and believed in the true God, Jesus Christ.
And the holy Soterichus began to confront the king.
He spoke with authority and released all the Christians who were imprisoned.
When King Herodian heard of it, he was furious; he spoke in haste and had Soterichus brought to him.

And when he came, the king said to him, "Soterichus, what is this audacity that you have committed in my kingdom? You have opposed my command concerning those whom it is right to worship as gods, though after me it is you who are first in my kingdom." Soterichus answered, "From now on I will never submit to a king of this world, but I will draw near to the true King, Jesus Christ, whose kingdom neither passes away nor comes to an end. Now therefore, O king, do not trouble me. I will not worship your abominable gods, nor will I forsake my King Jesus."
Soterichus answered, "From now on I will never submit to a king of this world, but I will draw near to the true King, Jesus Christ, whose kingdom neither passes away nor comes to an end.
Now therefore, O king,
When he had said these things, the king was furious and commanded that he be bound.
And when his soldiers saw him bound, they cried out, "Our lord, command us to set you free, and we will rescue you from the king."
He said to them, "No, for it is the will of my Lord Jesus that I die for his holy name.
Our Lord Jesus did not desire war, but peace.
For my part, this is what I ask of you:"
And they all cried out, "Whatever you say, we are ready to do it with joy."
Standing by him that day were five chiliarchs with their host of soldiers,
and they came to the king with one mind, saying, "We are all Christians. The death that our lord Soterichus is to die, we too will die."
When the king heard them, he was furious, and indeed deeply troubled.
He commanded that they be put into ships and taken out to the open sea. They cut off their heads and threw their bodies into the sea, while the holy Soterichus stood over them praying.
He looked and saw their souls going up to heaven like white doves.
Then he too stretched out his neck, and they took his head.
Their whole number was four hundred and fifty-six, together with the five chiliarchs, and they were all perfected on a single day, the ninth of Tobe, in peace. Amen.
Listen now, my brothers, and I will tell you that God does not forget those who are zealous [?] for him, but helps them and gives them strength.

Now after the holy Soterichus had been martyred, there was a soldier in the palace, thirty-three years old, whose name was Elias. He was handsome in face, mighty in strength, and perfect in every good work.
There was
This man was a physician who stood before the king at all times because of the healings he performed, so that whenever the king and his nobles fell ill, it was he who treated them.
For this reason all the people of the palace loved him, from the least to the greatest.
Now the holy Elias thought daily of the holy Soterichus,
and he would pray, saying, "When I am found worthy, may you reveal yourself to me, so that I may see your face again.
As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, the death that you died, I too will die."
As he was sleeping and thinking of these things, a voice came to him: "Elias, Elias."
He said, "Here I am, lord. Who are you that call me?"
The holy Elias thought that the king had fallen ill and had sent for him to heal him.

The voice came to him a second time: "My chosen one Elias, I am not an earthly king, as you suppose, who needs a physician to heal him. But open your eyes and know who I am. I am Jesus, the sweet fragrance of the incense of the Father.
I
I am Jesus, the sweet fragrance of the true vine of the good Father.
I am Jesus, the gladness of the water of the Acherusian Lake.
I am Jesus, the bond of the aeons that cannot be loosed.
I am Jesus, who helps everyone who believes in him with all their heart."
When the holy Elias heard these things, he lifted up his eyes and saw him mounted upon the chariots of the cherubim,
with Michael the archangel at his right hand and the holy Soterichus at his left, clothed in a precious garment such as no king of this world is able to wear.

When the holy Elias saw these things, he bowed down before the Lord, saying, "Forgive me, my Lord, for I am a sinful man. But I know, my Lord, that you grant repentance to the sinner if he turns and repents. I beseech you, therefore, my Lord Jesus Christ, who forgives all sinners: forgive me too all the sins I have committed while I did not know you."
I beseech you, therefore, my Lord Jesus Christ, who forgives all sinners: forgive me too all the sins I have committed while I did not know you.
And at that very hour he raised him up, saying to him, "Arise, my chosen one Elias. I am
Jesus, who helps you. Amen, I say to you, I will grant you my kingdom.

For I know that you will endure many sufferings for my name. But do not be afraid; they will not be able to prevail against you, for I am with you in every place to which they take you, giving you strength until you complete your contest.

When the king sends for you tomorrow, do not go to him as you usually do. He will send for you a second time, and they will compel you until they bring you to him. Then he will ask you, 'Why, when I sent for you, did you not come to me at once?' [Answer] Answer him boldly, without any fear, with the holy words that I will put into your mouth.
He will ask you, 'Why, when I sent for you,
Answer
And I am with you, and I will fill you with the Holy Spirit, giving you strength until my name is glorified through you.
Arise now; come, greet your companion Soterichus, whom you asked to see."
When the Saviour had said this to him, he gave him peace and went up to heaven in glory.
Likewise a great fragrance spread through the bedchamber in which the holy Elias was sleeping. At dawn
At dawn, when it turned out that the holy Elias had not gone to the king's palace,
the king sent for him. The messengers said to him, "The king is calling you, O Elias.
Why have you not come to the palace today?"
The holy man said to them, "Go and tell the king: Thus says Elias, the servant of Jesus Christ: From this moment I will not submit to you, for it is not right for the living to
submit to the dead; rather, the dead submits to the living, so that he too may live through him."
When the messengers heard these things from the holy Elias, they reported them to the king word for word.
When the king heard these things he was furious, and he sent a general to bring him to him against his will.
And when they had brought him to him,
the king said to him, "Elias, I love you dearly. Why have you held me in such utter contempt? You have scorned me."
The holy Elias said to him, "All the gods of the nations are silver and gold.
See, then, O king: you know that you are a mortal man, and yet you worship dead gods.

My God, Jesus Christ, is a living God, and everyone living who believes in him will live in him. Thus it is written: 'Just as my Father lives, I too live because of my Father; and you also will live because of me.'" When the king heard these things, he said, "Elias, listen to me and worship my gods, so that you may escape great and evil tortures."
Thus it is written: 'Just as my Father lives, I too live because of my Father; and you also will live because of me.'
When the king heard these things,
"Do you want to die the contemptible death of Soterichus?"
The saint said to him, "O king, the death of Soterichus is not a contemptible death; it is exceedingly honoured,
for thus it is written: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy one.'"
The king said to him, "Elias, my beloved, do not make me hate you to the utmost [?]."
But the holy Elias resolved to put the king's gods to shame.
He said, "O king, since you have pressed me so hard, I for my part do not wish to grieve you;
but I want you to let no one enter the temple until I have finished offering sacrifice to your gods."
So the king ordered that the holy Elias be allowed to go in.
Then the holy man took an axe with him under his clothes.

And when he saw the idols standing on their pedestals, he went up to them with great power from God and threw them down from their pedestals with the axe that was in his hand. He struck their heads off their bodies, and the angel of the Lord hung their bodies up in the air in the middle of the temple.
The angel of the Lord hung their bodies up in the air in the middle of the temple.
Their heads lay beside their pedestals.
Then the holy Elias came outside and said to the king, "O king, tell me about your gods,
for I went into the temple and did not find them there, so as to worship them,
since it is written in the Gospel: 'The Lord your God you shall worship, and him alone shall you serve.'"
When the king heard these things, he got up quickly and went into the temple, and he saw nothing but the heads lying beside their pedestals.
He ordered the priests to be brought to him and asked them, "Where are the gods, so that we may worship them?"
They were afraid and could not find anything to say; or rather, they wanted to deceive the king.
They said to the king, "O our lord the king, live for ever! The gods have fled from us, saying, 'Enemies of the king mean to rise up against him; we will go and wage the war and then return to you.'"
When the holy Elias heard these things, he rejoiced greatly and laughed: "So your gods forgot to take their heads with them when they went off to war!"

And when the king heard these things, he was deeply ashamed, or rather he grew furious with the priests. He said, "O you who deserve to be destroyed by the sword, do gods go to war with no heads on them?"
He said, "O you who deserve to be destroyed by the sword, do gods go to war with no heads on them?"

While the king was saying this, behold, a voice came out of the bodies of the idols hanging up in the air in the temple, saying, "O King Herodian, do not believe these priests who are deceiving you, saying that we have gone to war in order to save you. If we were gods, we would not lack the power to wage war.
If we were gods, we would not lack the power to wage war.

For behold, we are hanging in the midst of the air by the God of the holy Elias, and we have not been able to save ourselves; how then shall we save you? We beg you, O king, to ask the holy Elias to let us down, so that we may not stay like this.
We beg you, O king."
The king turned to the holy Elias and said to him, "Elias, I know that nothing is impossible for you; and when you were in the palace, you used to heal every sickness without difficulty.
So now I ask you to heal the gods, to stop them hanging up there, and to make their heads join their bodies again."
The holy Elias said to the king, "Do men heal gods, or do gods heal men?"
The king said to him, "Truly, God heals man."
The holy Elias said, "Truly, you have judged rightly.
Why then do you compel me to heal these gods of yours, calling them gods?
If they are gods, let them heal themselves.
But since you have asked me, O king, to let them down and stop them hanging, I will not grieve you."
And the holy Elias lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed,
saying, "Hear me, Jesus, the ear that hears, the eye that sees."
And at once the idols fell to the ground and were shattered, and they became like dust, together with their heads that lay on the ground.
Afterwards a strong wind blew and swept the dust of the idols away, and they were wiped off the earth.

When the king saw what had happened, he said to the saint, "O Elias, is this your gratitude for what I did for you, when I still held you in favour? You in turn have made my gods like dust before me."
The holy man said to the king, "It is written that the ungodly is like the dust which the wind drives from the face of the earth.
And you too, O king, if you remain ungodly…"
When the king heard these things, he was furious,
and he ordered that he be shut up until the next day.
But the holy Elias spent the whole night praying to God.
As for the king, while he was still asleep that night, behold, the devil came in to him in the form of a great black dragon, whose appearance was terrifying.
When the king saw him, he was troubled and cried out, "Who are you, O you whom I see in this form and this fearful shape?" The dragon answered, "I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.
The dragon answered, "I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.

Why have you let Elias go, this Christian magician who destroyed your gods? Do you want to become a Christian too and be my enemy? If so, I will punish you with a great vengeance; for behold, you see how fearsome I am."

The king was deeply troubled, for the dragon's eyes were flashing with fire. The king said to him, "My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do; only do not destroy me." The devil said to him, "If you will listen to me, when you get up early tomorrow, have them make you gods of gold in place of the stones that Elias destroyed.

The king said to him, "My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do; only do not destroy me." The devil said to him, "If you will listen to me, when you get up early tomorrow, have them make you gods of gold.
Said
And compel him too to worship them. If he disobeys you, torture him all the more."

When the dragon had said these things, he led the king's heart astray, and he became a flame of fire and flew away. And when the king got up early, he ordered them to make him gods of gold in place of the stones, just as the devil had said.
And when the king got up early, he ordered them to make him gods of gold in place of the stones, just as the devil had said.
Then he had the holy Elias brought to him.

The king said to him, "What will you say to me now? Will you be able to say of these that they are not gods? Behold, I have made them of gold. So now listen to me: come and worship them before I torture you, for I will not spare you a single day longer."
The holy Elias said to the king, "Do quickly whatever you want with me,
for I will not forsake my Lord Jesus Christ to worship things made by human hands."
When the king heard these things, he was furious, and he ordered them to break open his legs with swords and draw out their bones.
The king said to him, "Elias, you have seen the beginning of the tortures, how very cruel they are. So listen to me and escape this cruel torture."
The saint said to him, "I do not care about your tortures, O son of the devil."
When the king heard these things, he was furious, and he ordered them to pull out his nails, one by one, from his hands and his feet.
The king said to him, "Listen to me, so that you may escape cruel tortures: sacrifice, and I will release you."
The holy Elias said, "You have done me a good thing now, O king,
for thus it is written: 'Where is your sting, O death?' And the sting of death is sin."
When the king realized that this torture had not harmed him,
he ordered them to strip the skin from his ribs and pull out his sinews one by one.
These are the tortures that they inflicted on him that day.
The king said, "O Elias, there is yet another torture that I will give you. If you do not sacrifice, by the welfare of my kingdom, I will kill you with a cruel death."

The holy Elias said to him, "It is written: 'Do not fear those who will kill your body; but your soul they have no power to destroy.'" When the king heard these things, he ordered that he be laid on a bed of iron.
These

And they poured pitch [?] over his body. But he did not feel this terrible torture; instead he was reciting this psalm: "The saints will boast in glory and honour; they will rejoice upon their beds, with the exaltation of God in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands."
He was reciting this psalm: "The saints will boast in glory and honour; they will rejoice upon their beds, with the exaltation of God in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands."
When the king saw that he had not felt this torture either,
the king at once rose from the tribunal and went down to the sea.
He had the holy Elias brought to him, together with two very fierce wild beasts: a [?]

and a she-bear with cubs. The king ordered that a small [?] boat be brought to him, and he had all its tackle removed. He had the holy Elias put aboard it with the beasts, and had it towed out into the middle of the open sea, tied to the [?]. Then they cut the boat's ropes and left it drifting in the middle of the open sea, with the holy Elias aboard it together with the beasts.
He turned his face toward the east and prayed, saying: "I beseech you, Jesus, Son of the living God, who saved Daniel from the mouths of the lions:
save me too from the hands of the wild beasts.
You are the one who saved the prophet Jonah when he was in the belly of the sea monster:
save me too in the middle of this raging open sea."
While the holy Elias was still praying, he saw that the beasts too had turned their faces to the east and were crying out to God in their own language.

The righteous man turned again and prayed, saying: "You who guided Joseph, guide me too, along with these two irrational animals, in the midst of these [?]. For just as they have cast me adrift, so they have cast these adrift too; and see, they are glorifying your holy name."
At that very hour Michael and Gabriel came down from heaven. They went to him, greeted him and said to him: "Be strong, holy Elias! No one can do you any harm.
We have been sent to you to steer your boat until we bring you to the country of Kounthia, for a great contest awaits you there."
While the angels were speaking with him, one of them sat at the prow of the boat
and the other steered it. At once they came to the borders of Kounthia.
And the angels of the Lord greeted him and went up to heaven in glory, in the peace of God. Amen.
This is the first martyrdom of the holy Elias, which he underwent under Hierodianus, king of Thentike [?], in peace. [?]
Now Liberianus, the king of Kounthia, came out to the sea. He looked out over it and saw the little boat floating on the sea,
with the holy Elias aboard it and the beasts licking his feet. At once the king ordered
that it be brought into the harbor.
He saw the holy Elias with his face beaming with joy, and the king said to him: "What country are you from? Where do you come from?"
The holy man said to him: "I am a man of Thentike [?], and I belong to Christ."
When King Liberianus heard the name of Jesus, he was greatly troubled, since he himself was a worshipper of idols.
He said: "You are truly one of the Christian magicians.
Well then, here are the signs of your magic, plain to see: if you were not a magician, you would not have been saved from these fierce beasts.
But I am the one who will torture you as your magic deserves."
The devil had put it into his heart to do great harm to the holy man. The king ordered that he be bound with iron chains and thrown into a bronze [?] until the next day, when he would hear his case,
and he had the beasts taken away to the hunting arena.
Early the next morning the king ordered that the holy Elias be brought to him in the theater of the city, so that he might hear his case in public.
When the king first [?] him, he asked him: "What is your name?" The saint said to him: "My name according to the world is Elias, but my name in the Spirit is the one given to me by Jesus Christ."
The king said to him: "So you have two names, unlike everyone else?"
The saint said to him: "I am not the only one who has two names. Everyone who believes in my God is changed in his strength

and receives a name according to the Spirit. For what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. That is why there is one name according to the flesh and another according to the Spirit."
When the king heard this, he said: "Elias, these words will do you no good [?]. You will die a miserable death,
and no one will be able to save you from my hands."
The holy Elias said to him: "I would rather die at your hands
than disobey Jesus my God."
When the king heard this,

he ordered that his ribs be scraped with iron claws and his feet with knives. While they were scraping him, the king shouted at him: "Obey me and sacrifice, so that I may spare you from great tortures."
But the holy man said nothing at all; he only looked up to heaven.
When the king saw that he did not feel it, he ordered that he be thrown into a cauldron full of boiling oil and that a fire be kindled under it for two hours,
so that his body was thoroughly cooked. After that they poured sulfur and pitch over him,
and the flames rose seventy cubits above his body.
The king thought that he was already dead.
Then he cried out: "O Elias, where is Jesus your God? Let him save you from my hands now!"

But the holy man was filled with the Holy Spirit while he was in the fire, and he cried out, saying: "Shut your mouth and be silent, lawless king, you who speak the name of my God with your defiled mouth!" When the king heard that he was not dead, he was utterly astonished,
and he struck his hands together
and said: "Truly I know that I will not get the better of you [?] until I undo your magic. I will send for a magician who is more skilled than you, and he will undo your magic,

and then I will punish you." He had him thrown into a cell and hung up upside down, with his head lowered into a jar full of vinegar and lye, the lye reaching up to his chest. He sealed the door with his ring until he could send for the magician and bring him to test Elias against him.
When the king had gone outside the place where the holy Elias was shut in,
behold, Michael the archangel came to the holy Elias. He took him down from where he hung, sealed his body with the sign of the cross, and made it as though it had never been touched at all.
He also brought him some of the fruit of the trees of paradise to eat,
for he had eaten nothing since the day they put him out on the sea with the beasts.
Michael said to him: "Be strong, O holy Elias, [?] victor, crowned champion, our friend, fellow heir of Jesus Christ.
Truly I tell you, they have already prepared your
throne in the seventh place at the right hand of Christ. Do not be afraid: I will stay with you and help you wherever they take you."
When the angel of the Lord had said this to him, he went up to heaven in glory.
The king sent for a great master magician named Theocletus, who was famous throughout the whole country of Kounthia. When he came to him,
the king said to him: "Theocletus, I have heard of your fame, that you are a master magician.
Now then, let your mastery be shown on this Christian.
For I have heard that they have a god called Jesus, and whenever they invoke his name he helps them in every need."
When Theocletus the magician heard this, he laughed and said to the king: "Do not let such talk trouble you. I will show you that I have the power to undo the magic of the Christians."
The magician rose and took the king outside the palace.
They went into a tomb.
He turned his face to the west
and invoked the keeper of Tartarus, saying: "Send me up a soul to tell the king that I am able to undo the magic of the Christians."
At once the keeper of Tartarus came up with a multitude of souls, bound and being tortured. The magician asked the keeper of Tartarus to open the mouth of one soul so that it could speak.

When they allowed the soul to speak, it cried out, saying: "Woe to you, King Liberianus! Woe to everyone who denies this name, Jesus! And as for you, Theocletus the magician, you do not have the power to contend with Elias the Christian.

Yet blessed are you, for you will be saved through him, and you will receive what your name means: 'the one whom God has saved.' You will try to do Elias harm, but he will do you good; you will try to kill him, but he will give you life. But I adjure you by the grace that will come upon you: when you receive life through the holy Elias, remember me too before him,
so that he may perhaps entreat his God Jesus to rescue us from the punishments we are in. For we are tortured all the more because we denied him in our ignorance while we were in the world.
Now we know that this Jesus is a merciful God, who forgives the sins of all who turn to him with an upright heart."

When the king heard these words, he said: "What are you going to do to Elias the Christian, who has made demons appear in an apparition and speak these false words so that we would be afraid and spare him?" The magician answered and said to the king: "Do not think that the words this soul has spoken to us are false.

This soul said that I have no power to contend with Elias the Christian because his God fights for him, and I believe the word is true. For I once heard about some magicians of old, men of Egypt, two brothers, one named Jannes
and the other Jambres, who opposed a man named Moses
and could not prevail against him,
because his God fought for him.
So now we too, O king, have gone astray in our folly; for no one can prevail against anyone for whom God fights.
But I do not wish to grieve you, O king. I will test Elias the Christian three times. If I cannot prevail against him, then truly no one has power over him."
Then the king went into the chamber where the holy man was shut in, and found the seal he had set on it intact.
The king was saying: "Perhaps you will find that he has already died from the torture I left him in."
But when he opened the door and went in, he smelled a great fragrance in the chamber. He looked and saw the holy Elias standing in prayer, surrounded by great glory.
When the king saw this he was astonished; yet the devils kept leading his heart astray,
and he ordered that the holy Elias be brought out. The magician said
to the king: "Let us take this Christian
up the mountain, away from these crowds, and test each other at once."
So the king went up the mountain with the magician and the holy man.
The king said to him: "O Elias, I have brought you up this mountain to test you today." The holy man said to him: "I do not know what magic is; but the power of Jesus my God is invincible."
The king turned to the magician and said to him: "Whatever you are going to do, do it quickly."
The magician stood and made his invocation, and the mountain split in two,
and two great, very fierce dragons came up. But the holy Elias did not look at them at all; he stood praying to God.
When the dragons saw the holy Elias praying, they were stopped short
and stood still like creatures afraid to approach him. When the magician saw this, he was utterly astonished. He labored at his invocations, but the dragons did not move from their place.
The magician, wanting to please the king, said: "O Elias, do you think you have held back the dragons
and kept them from approaching you because my art has failed? Look, I tell you: I will do you worse harm than this."

After that he made an invocation over the dragons, and they split open down the middle. He took the dragons' gall, their [?] and their liver, along with a dead [?] and a wild [?], and mixed them together.
He put them in a new cup and invoked over them the names of demons,
so that the abyss split open and the devil came up, and the whole mountain was filled with demons in apparitions.
When the king saw this, he was overjoyed,

and he seized the magician's head and kissed it, saying: "Truly I know that you are able to undo the magic of the Christians." The magician mixed the unclean things together, put them into the cup, and held it out to the righteous man. When he took it, he said: "I do not want to drink these unclean things;

but it is of no concern to me, for it is written in scripture: Even if they drink a deadly poison, it will not harm them." Then the holy Elias looked up to heaven and prayed, saying: "Hear me, my Lord Jesus Christ, who hears everyone who cries out to him, who heard Abraham in his sojourning,
who saved Isaac from the hands of the Philistines,
who saved Jacob from the hands of Esau, who saved Joseph from the hand of Potiphar's wife,
who saved Moses from the hands of Pharaoh
and from the hands of Jannes and Jambres:
I beseech you, I your servant Elias, to save me from these apparitions. Do not let them prevail over me, so that the enemy may not boast over me.
For I have heard in the holy scripture: If God is the one who fights for us, who can stand against us? And again Elisha says: Those who fight for us are more than those who stand against us.

Now then, my Lord Jesus Christ, who saved Elisha from the hand of the king of Syria, save me too from the hand of these demons." And when the blessed Elias had finished praying, behold, Michael the archangel came to him, scourged all the demons and drove them off the mountain.
And the devil himself turned into a flame of fire and flew away. The king did not see the angel, but only the holy Elias.
When the holy Elias saw the angel standing beside him, he was overjoyed. He sealed himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
and drank the cup full of uncleanness, and no harm at all came to him.
On the contrary, his face was cheerful, like a man merry with wine.
When Publianus saw that no harm had come to the holy Elias,
he raised his hands and cried out, saying: "Truly there is no god in heaven or on earth like Jesus Christ [?], the God of the holy Elias!"
The magician answered, saying: "There is one more thing by which I will test you.
If no harm comes to you, then truly your God is the true one."
At once the magician made an invocation, and a great rock of fire rose up on the mountain before them.
He said to the righteous man: "If you trust your God with all your heart, that Jesus is a mighty God, then come and go into this rock of fire.
And if no harm comes to you, then I too will believe in your God."
The holy Elias lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed, saying: "I entreat you, Jesus, with whom nothing is impossible.
I entreat you, Jesus, hope of those who trust in him; I entreat you, Jesus, boast of the righteous, crown of the martyrs. You said in the holy scriptures: Fire will not harm you.
And again you said: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. So I am confident that you have power in all things.

You who saved the three holy ones from the blazing furnace, save me too, so that your glory may be revealed before this magician and Publianus the senator." [?] At once clouds of dew came out of heaven and covered the saint's body like a garment.
He sealed himself and went into the fire,
and he spent two hours in the middle of the fire, praying. After that he came out of the fire.
No harm whatever had come to him; there was not even the smell of fire on his clothes.
The magician and the senator went to him and greeted him, saying: "Truly your God Jesus is the true God,
and nothing is impossible for him. We entreat you, O holy Elias, to pray to your God that he may grant us your crown of Christianity."

The holy Elias was overjoyed. He spread out his hands and prayed, saying: "I entreat you, my Lord Jesus Christ, the God who forgives: forgive Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator. You said: I do not desire the death of the sinner so much as that he turn and repent.
And again you said: I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Now then, I entreat you to let this rock of fire be changed and become a spring of water, so that I may baptize those you have chosen in your holy name,
and they may receive the seal of life. You said to your disciples: Go out into the whole world and baptize all the nations in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit."
And at that very hour
the rock of fire was changed
and became a spring of water, surging with waves.
And the holy Elias baptized Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator,
and sealed them in the name of the Father and the Son
and the Holy Spirit, for the forgiveness of their sins.
When the king saw this, he was furious that the magician and the senator had believed in the Lord Jesus. He came down the mountain with them,
and he ordered that the magician and the senator be beheaded together.
Publianus the senator had three friends, who came to visit him and found him in chains.

They said to him: "What is this that has happened to you, our friend? Has the king seized you over money you could not pay? If so, we will give you whatever the king has seized you for." He said to them: "If you are willing to listen to me, your friend, do what I tell you.

I ask nothing of you except that you confess the God of the holy Elias, so that you may receive the crown that never perishes." At once they cried out: "We are ready to die for his holy name!" And they all cried out to the king: "We are Christians!" Publius the senator was there with his three friends, his soldiers and his household, and Theocletus the magician as well. The king ordered that pits be dug and filled with fire, and that the holy ones be thrown into them,

and he burned them all on a single day. This is how Publius the senator, Theocletus the magician and all who were with them, nine hundred and seventy-four in number, completed their martyrdom on the twentieth of Mechir [?]; they went up to heaven in glory.
After this they brought the holy Elias before the tribunal.
The king said to him: "Elias, do you think that because you killed my magician I will be afraid of you and let you go?
By the might of my kingship,
I will torture you cruelly until I see whether Jesus can save you from my hands."
But the holy Elias kept completely silent;
he only looked up to heaven.
The king ordered that they drive red-hot awls,
two into his ears and two more into his eyes,
and afterward cut out his tongue,
so that his brain was cooked. After that he ordered him to be laid on a bed
of iron, and molten lead to be poured into his mouth.
But the holy Elias rose up under this torture in a [?]
…courage.
After this he had them flay the skin of his head and torture him.

And the holy one rose up from under yet another torture. After this he ordered them to dig a pit down into the ground, the size of his length and his breadth, and had them lower the holy one down into it. After this he had them light a fire under a cauldron full of lead until it became like water, and they turned the windlass and poured it down over his body until it came up to his neck. At once Michael the archangel stood over him and would not let the fire or the molten lead touch him at all; instead it was like cold water upon him.
When the king saw that he paid him no heed, he grew very angry.
The king rose, took his own knife, and with his own hand pierced the righteous man's heart, and his bowels fell down onto the ground.
At once, behold, a cloud of light overshadowed him, and the angel of the Lord took his bowels and put them back inside him before his eyes,
and he anointed his whole body, and he became as though they had never touched him at all.
When the king saw that he could not prevail over him,

he said, "I know what I will do: I will send him to Eutychodorus. Perhaps he has a magician with him who is very powerful." He rose there from the tribunal and ordered them to shut him in until he had written his report.
And he took a sheet of papyrus and wrote on it as follows: "I, Liberianus, king of Kounthia, write to Eutychodorus, king of the Medes: greetings.
Since the race of the Christians has risen in revolt with works of magic deserving of death,
behold, I have sent you one of them, whose name is Elias, so that you may put him to death."
Then he ordered them to bring out the holy Elias and hand him over to two protectors. They embarked and set sail on the sea, and they bound Saint Elias and threw him down into the hold of the ship.
When they had set out [?], Michael came down from heaven with a cloud of light. He went down into the hold of the ship, set Saint Elias free, and placed him on the cloud of light,
and carried him up to heaven.
He saw all the saints and greeted them, and they rejoiced over him. He carried him up to the third heaven,
and also into paradise, with the tree of life in its midst.
Again he brought him into the land of the inheritance.
He saw it: its soil was white like refined silver, and it bore countless fruits, exceedingly good.
Again they brought him to the city of Christ,
and twelve walls surrounded that city.
Again they showed him a great house like a royal palace, built within the wall, about fifteen stadia in breadth, built entirely of gold and pearls, and about a hundred cubits in height.
Its gates were built of precious stones and shone more brightly than the sun.

Michael said to him, "Saint Elias, this house built of gold and pearls is yours." When the holy Elias heard these words, he rejoiced greatly. And as he was walking in the city, behold, the Lord Jesus came out of heaven before him.
He said to him, "Be strong, O Elias, my beloved. Your contest has drawn near to you. Behold, you have seen how many good things I have prepared for those who will believe in me with all their heart.

I am Jesus, the joy of all the ages. Behold, I too rejoice with you today. As for you, my beloved, when they bring you to Media, Eutychodorus king of Media will put you to death, for it is through him that you will complete your contest."
Saint Elias answered and said to the Savior, "My Lord, I do not want to enter into the midst of the godless heathen, lest they scatter my bones and wipe out my memory from the earth."

The Savior said to him, "Truly I say to you, O my chosen Elias, just as the dew of heaven spreads over the whole earth, so will my name be glorified through you, because of the mighty works that will take place through your body.
And because you have asked me that your body be taken away from the heathen, I will set your heart at rest and fulfill your request.
After some days I will reveal your memory in a vision to righteous men who live in Egypt, and I will have them come for your body and carry it up to Egypt and lay it there.
And in the place where your body will be laid, I will have them lay the bodies of other righteous men,
two of them, there with you.
And the place where your body will be laid will become a temple for me forever.
And whoever comes into your shrine and asks me for any request in faith, in your name, I will grant it to him.
And anyone suffering from any sickness who comes into your shrine and entreats you in my name, I will grant them healing [?], and I will make your
name renowned everywhere, and I will cause great mighty works and wonders to take place in your resting place."
When the Lord Jesus had said these things, he went up to heaven in glory.
And at once the ship put in at the harbor of Media, the metropolis of the Medes,
and the protectors gave the letters to King Eutychodorus.
The second martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he underwent under Liberianus, king of Kounthia. In peace. Amen.

Now when they had delivered the report about Saint Elias to Eutychodorus, king of Media, he read everything that had been written to him and had him shut in until the next day, so that he could give him a hearing. He wrote letters in reply and sent them off
so that they might go back to their king, to their own country. The next day the king sat on the tribunal and had them bring the holy Elias to him.

The king said to him, "Elias, there are these evil deeds which have been written to me, that you do them. Now then, sacrifice." The righteous man answered, "It is written in the holy Scriptures: 'You shall not worship things made by hands, for I am God, and there is no other
besides me.'" When the king heard this, he had him hung up in a linen tunic, and they shot arrows at him for three hours.
But the holy Elias sealed himself with the sign of the cross.
At once, behold, a cloud of light covered him, and not a single arrow touched him at all.
When the king saw this, he was greatly amazed and ordered them to take him down from the wood.

The king said to him, "Elias, I want you to tell me about this sign which you made on your forehead, so that you were saved from these arrows. For I say in my heart that what you did is a work of magic; otherwise you would not have been saved." Saint Elias said to him, "O king, do not think that what I did is a work of magic, far from it! This is the sign of the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ." The king said to him, "They hanged your Lord? What did they do to him?"

The righteous man said to him, "He went up on the cross and died for our sins." The king said to him, "So your god died too, like any man?" The righteous man said, "Not at all. He is immortal; he died, but he rose again, so that he might give us life." The king said to him, "Truly, the death by which your god Jesus died is the death by which I will kill you too."
Then he ordered them to make a cross and hang the holy one on it. When they had set the holy one on it, he rejoiced, because he had been found worthy of the likeness of the Lord.
And at once, behold, a dove of light settled on the right arm of the cross,
and another on the left arm, and they spread their wings over him and covered him, for he was naked.
And behold, a voice came to him: "O Elias, behold the likeness which I bore, I the Son of God; behold, you too have borne it.
For they hanged me on the cross and placed me between two thieves. Truly I say to you, my chosen Elias, there is nothing greater than the likeness which you have borne."
And when Jesus had finished speaking with him, there were thunders and lightnings, and a great fear
fell upon everyone around him.
And behold, the angels came, set the holy one free, and brought him down from the cross. They took the cross and sped away, leaving Saint Elias standing.

When the king saw these things, he was amazed. He rose from the tribunal that day and had him shut in until the next day. The next day, because the king was very angry, since the devil had filled his heart with every evil against him, he at once sat on the tribunal and ordered them to bring the holy one to him. The king said to him, "Elias, do you think that because you practiced arts of magic until you were saved from the cross, there are no more tortures left for you?" The king ordered them to break the joints of his hands and of his feet,
and he endured it.
And he had them beat his head with an iron hammer until his brain came out through his mouth and his nostrils.
When the king saw that he had not died from all the things he had done to him,
he had them bring him wild beasts, exceedingly fierce: a leopard and a wild boar.
He had Saint Elias thrown to them, thinking that they would tear him open at once.

When the beasts saw Saint Elias praying to God, they ran to him wagging their tails at him, and they bowed down and worshiped him. The king was greatly amazed and knew that he could not prevail over him. He passed sentence on him, that they should cut off his head and carry him to an island in the sea and leave him there. As they were about to lead Saint Elias out to cut off his head, he turned his face to the east and prayed thus: "I bless you, my Lord Jesus Christ, because I have been found worthy to come to this hour, to die for your holy name. I beseech you, my Lord, do not put me to shame as I come to you."
At once the sweet voice of the Lord came to him: "Truly I say to you, O my chosen Elias, the will of my Father has been fulfilled in your contest.
Behold, my heavens have been adorned with crowns before you. Victorious is he who has conquered; mighty is he who has prevailed."
When the holy Elias heard this, he sealed himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
and stretched out his neck, and they took off his head at the ninth hour on the fifteenth of Paremhat.
The angels and all the saints came out before him and greeted him,
and they sang the hymn of Alleluia until they had brought him to the city of Christ.
When they had taken off his head, they took his body and laid it on an island in the middle of the sea,

until the day when God revealed him in a vision to two righteous monks in the land of Egypt, that they should go for his body, bring it to Egypt, and lay it in the place which the Lord had prepared for him. This is how he completed his martyrdom. He went up to heaven in glory and received the incorruptible crown. In peace. Amen.

All those who were martyred with Saint Elias received the crown of everlasting life. They number six thousand four hundred and thirty souls, and with Saint Elias they entered into life. May their holy blessing be with us. Amen.
And this is how the holy Elias completed his honored contest on the fifteenth of Paremhat, having fallen into the hands of three kings, who are these:
Herodianus, king of the Enetoi [?], and Saint Elias was a native of that country;
the second is Liberianus, king of Kounthia; the third is Eutychodorus, king of the Medes, through whom he was made perfect and went up to heaven in glory and honor.
May it come to pass that we too attain the good things of the kingdom of heaven, through the grace
and love for humankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, life-giving and consubstantial, now and always, forever and ever. Amen.
